source_units.source_assertion: Lilly says that he has long favored Dariot’s method of judging sickness and has annexed an abridged, shorter presentation of it.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: The full italic introduction belongs to the span. “Some abbreviation” and the comparison with what was published before are authorial descriptions, not a claim that this is an unaltered translation or a complete reproduction of Dariot.

point_of_use.section: If the Party be sicke of whom the Question is Demanded
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: If the Party be sicke of whom the Question is Demanded.
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: The first question is whether the person about whom the question is asked is sick.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: This heading establishes the question of sickness status; it is not yet a rule for a disease’s quality or duration.
source_units.attribution: Heading preceding the marginal label Dariot

point_of_use.section: Sickness status: Dariot
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: THE Significator of the Querent in a Signe contrary to his owne nature ... as [Mars] being Lord of the ascendant ... in [Cancer] ... or if the Lord of the ascendant be in a Cadent house, chiefly in the sixt, he is sick.
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: A significator in a sign contrary to its own nature is a sickness indication. Mars, lord of the ascendant, naturally hot and dry, in cold and moist Cancer is the example. The alternative is the lord of the ascendant in a cadent house, especially the sixth.
source_units.antecedents_and_scope: Querent’s significator in contrary-nature sign; OR ascendant lord cadent.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: “Chiefly” gives special emphasis to the sixth; it does not restrict the cadent-house assertion to the sixth. Mars/Cancer is an illustrative configuration, not a patient case.
source_units.attribution: Dariot, explicit marginal label

point_of_use.section: Sickness status: Dariot
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: A diurnall Planet being Significator, and he under the earth, ill affected, Combust, Retrograde; in his Fall or Detriment, weak, or in Terms of malevolents, or with violent fixed Stars, or besieged by the two Infortunes ... What was spoken of a diurnall Planet, must be understood of a nocturnall one (consideratis considerandis.)
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: The text lists adverse states of a diurnal significator and says that, these happening, the party is sick. It extends what has been said to a nocturnal planet with the requisite matters considered.
source_units.antecedents_and_scope: Diurnal significator; printed sequence: under earth, ill affected, combust, retrograde, fall/detriment, weak, malefics’ terms, violent fixed stars, or besieged by both infortunes.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: The printed list mixes conjunction and disjunction and is not an explicit Boolean checklist. The nocturnal extension is qualified by “consideratis considerandis”; the page does not explicitly spell out a replacement above-earth condition or all adjustments.
source_units.attribution: Dariot, continuing marginally attributed block

point_of_use.section: Sickness status: Lilly’s addition
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: When a Question was asked of me upon any Urine, or without it, having erected my Figure, I observed this method, to know whether the Querent was ill or no.
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: Lilly introduces his own procedure for a question brought with urine or without it, after erecting a figure, to determine whether the querent was ill.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: Urine is optional. This is a generalized practice statement; it identifies no individual consultation, date, or figure.
source_units.attribution: Lilly, explicit marginal label

point_of_use.section: Sickness status: Lilly’s condition chain
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: If the ascendant were not afflicted, or the Lord thereof out of his essentiall Dignities, or in any evill aspect of [Saturn] or [Mars], or Lord of the sixt. Or if no Planet afflicted the sixt house by presence, or that the [Moon] were not afflicted in the eighth or twelfth
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: These are the printed opening conditions of Lilly’s no-sickness judgment. The first is explicitly an unafflicted ascendant; later branches explicitly mention no planet afflicting the sixth by presence and the Moon not afflicted in the eighth or twelfth.
source_units.antecedents_and_scope: The entire printed negative chain must travel with the ensuing conclusion in SF-008. The ascendant-lord clauses read “out of” essential dignities and “in any evill aspect” without a separately printed “not.”
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: Do not silently add a negative, invert “out of,” or present the chain as an unambiguous formal rule. “Or” predominates; the page supplies no scoring or combination threshold.
source_units.attribution: Lilly, continuing explicit marginal attribution

point_of_use.section: Sickness status: Lilly’s positive alternatives
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: or if I found [Jupiter] or [Venus] or [North Node] in the ascendant, or the [Sun] in the sixt, or the [Moon] and Lord of the ascendant in any good aspect, or [Jupiter] or [Venus] casting a [trine] or [sextile] to the cusp of the ascendant or sixt house
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: Further alternatives in the no-sickness chain are Jupiter, Venus, or the North Node in the ascendant; the Sun in the sixth; Moon and ascendant lord in a good aspect; or Jupiter or Venus trine/sextile the ascendant or sixth cusp.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: The Sun-in-sixth clause is favorable here. Keep the cusp targets, the North Node, and “any good aspect” distinct; do not replace this with a generic benefic-strength condition.
source_units.attribution: Lilly, continuing explicit marginal attribution

point_of_use.section: Sickness status: Lilly’s conclusion
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: I would directly acquaint the party they were not sick, or that no sicknesse would succeed upon this Quere ... some sudden distemper of Body, which would presently be rectified.
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: Lilly says he would tell the party either that they were not sick or that no sickness would follow this query, and that their suspicion arose from a sudden bodily distemper that would soon be rectified.
source_units.antecedents_and_scope: Conclusion of SF-006 and SF-007, including their unresolved negative scope.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: Retain both alternatives: present non-sickness and no ensuing sickness. “Sudden distemper” is not no bodily disturbance at all. “Presently” gives no numeric duration.
source_units.attribution: Lilly, continuing explicit marginal attribution
source_units.evidence_character: reported habitual judgment, not an independently documented outcome

point_of_use.section: Cause of the Disease inward or outward: inward
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: The inward cause and condition of the Disease we require from the ill disposition of the Significator, in Signe, House and place of Heaven, his good or ill configuration with the malevolent Planets
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: The inward cause and condition are sought in the significator’s ill disposition by sign, house, and heavenly place, and in its good or ill configuration with malevolent planets.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: Both “good or ill” configurations are explicitly named; this is a method of interpretation in the source, not a physiological explanation established by cases.
source_units.attribution: Dariot, fresh explicit marginal label at printed259

point_of_use.section: Inward cause: functional malignancy
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: where generally observe, any Planet may in this case be malignant, if he be Lord of the eighth, twelfth or sixt, &c.
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: Any planet may be malignant in this context by being lord of the eighth, twelfth, or sixth, with an open “etc.”
source_units.antecedents_and_scope: Functional house rulership in this disease judgment.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: “May” is modal, and “any Planet” includes planets otherwise treated as benefic. The source does not close the set after the three named houses.

point_of_use.section: Outward cause: sources of judgment
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: The outward cause is required from those Infortunes that doe afflict the Lord of the ascendant, or from the principall Significators in the Figure, or the [Moon]
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: The outward cause is investigated through the infortunes afflicting the ascendant lord, with principal figure significators and the Moon also named in the printed sequence.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: The syntax does not clearly distribute the verb “afflict” across every subsequent noun. Preserve the named objects rather than reducing the rule to one fixed planet.
source_units.attribution: Dariot, continuing attributed explanation

point_of_use.section: Outward cause: strong ascendant lord
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: if you find the Lord of the ascendant sufficiently strong in essentiall Dignities, swift in motion, in a good house of Heaven, you may then judge the Querent is not naturally ill, but accidentally and outwardly afflicted
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: With the ascendant lord sufficiently strong in essential dignities, swift, and in a good house, the astrologer may judge accidental/outward affliction rather than natural illness.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: Three qualities are named together. “Sufficiently,” “good house,” and “may” are not quantified. The source distinguishes kinds of affliction; it does not declare the person entirely unaffected.
source_units.attribution: Dariot, continuing attributed explanation

point_of_use.section: Outward cause: malefic aspect with exclusions
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: notwithstanding the strength of the Lord of the ascendant ... either [Saturn] or [Mars] have some [square] or [opposition] aspect unto him, and neither of them be Lords of the sixt, or Dispositors of the [Moon] ... he is not well, yet not perfectly sick
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: Despite the strong ascendant lord, a Saturn or Mars square/opposition can be interpreted as an outward event making the person unwell, though not fully sick, when neither malefic is sixth lord or Moon dispositor.
source_units.antecedents_and_scope: Carry forward the ascendant-lord strength; Saturn or Mars square/opposition to that lord; exclusion of sixth lordship and Moon disposition for the named malefics.
source_units.qualifications_polarity_modality_referen: Both exclusions matter. “May judge” remains permissive. “Not well, yet not perfectly sick” is the source’s intermediate status, not equivalent to either complete health or inevitable disease.
source_units.attribution: Dariot, continuing attributed explanation

point_of_use.section: Outward cause: house interpretation
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: observe in what house that Planet is, or of what house he is Lord, and from the judgments belonging to that house, require satisfaction in Art; as for example

source_units.source_assertion: Determine the outward circumstance by the afflicting planet’s occupied house or house lordship, using the judgments appropriate to that house.

point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: If you find the Lord of the ascendant casually afflicted by Saturne or Mars, &c. and either of them are Lords of the second house, and there appears no inward cause of a Disease ... want of money, (if the Significators apply,) or hath had lately damage, if the Significators are separated

point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: the greatnesse or smalnesse of his losse judge according to the strength of the Planet afflicting, and quality of the aspect; where note, Oppositions herein worse then [square] aspects or Conjunctions
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.source_assertion: Judge loss magnitude by the afflicting planet’s strength and the aspect’s quality. In this context oppositions are worse than squares or conjunctions.

point_of_use.section: Outward cause: fifth-house example
point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: If it be the Lord of the fift, be the Planet good or ill, that afflicts ... either by evill Dyet, Surfet, &c. or by losse at Dice, Tables or Sports (if the Querent be capable) or that the Father comes not off freely with his Pension; (this is when young people demand a Question, or are distempered)
point_of_use.anchor_convention: Visually read source excerpt; long s is represented as s. Planet and aspect names may replace glyphs inside square brackets. Ellipses mark omitted intervening words, not a continuous transcription.

source_units.attribution: Lilly, continuing example

point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: if it be the Lord of the seventh that oppresses the Lord of the ascendant ... some difference with his Wife (and so a Woman, on the contrary, with her Husband,) or some Law-suit, or wilfull Neighbour-contention, or Partner is the outward cause

source_units.attribution: Lilly, continuing example

point_of_use.anchor_excerpt: in Youth, if the like configuration be upon the Question from the Lord of the seventh to the Lord of the ascendant, it’s alone melancholy; his Friend, or the Maid he affects, or the man he longs after is unkind ... yet will no sicknesse follow it
